clue.text: People still content ?

definitions.meaning: an old name for the people of Scotland, used as a plural noun
what comes out of a distillery's still: whisky from north of the border

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a dated collective name for the Scots and also the whisky distilled in their country.

clue.text: Bound over plain ?

definitions.meaning: to jump over something without touching it, as a horse does a fence
obvious, easy to see or understand

explanation.definitionFit: To leap a fence is to get over it cleanly; and something obvious is evident or transparent.

clue.text: Set up by Indians to time the French

parts.note: tempo is the time or speed of a piece of music
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Native Americans arranging to keep time with the French.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe before 'time' is an OCR blemish; the page prints plain 'time'. The definition is descriptive: the carved post was erected by Native American peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved, painted post bearing tribal emblems was erected by Indigenous peoples of north-west America.

clue.text: Lies about us at first, according to Wordsworth

definitions.text: Lies about us at first, according to Wordsworth

parts.words: Lies about us at first, according to Wordsworth
parts.note: Wordsworth's Immortality Ode says that paradise surrounds us in our infancy

explanation.surface: A poet accusing people of fibbing about us early on.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is 'Heaven lies about us in our infancy' from the Ode: Intimations of Immortality; 'lies about' means surrounds, not tells untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's ode says that paradise, the blessed abode, surrounds the newborn in early childhood.

clue.text: Bad player leaves all of their number standing

definitions.text: Bad player leaves all of their number standing

parts.words: Bad player leaves all of their number standing
parts.note: a skittles game played with nine wooden pins; a hopeless bowler knocks down none of the nine

explanation.surface: A poor team member who leaves all the rest still on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their number' looks like people, but it is the count of pins, nine, in an old skittles game.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles played with nine pins: a duff bowler leaves every one of the nine upright.

clue.text: Novel by a Brontë? Wrong — it's about a sword

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are wrapped about the sword
the letters of 'by a Brontë' are wrongly arranged, so they are shuffled

parts.note: a hanger is a short sword once worn hanging from the belt

explanation.surface: Someone credits a book to a Brontë sister and is told they are wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' is literally true: the book is Jane Austen's. The anagram of BYABRONTE gives NORT ... ABBEY, which goes about HANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's Gothic parody, published in 1817, is a famous English novel.

clue.text: Film gives four points on dance

parts.note: the four compass points north, east, west and south give N, E, W and S
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A movie offering four points about dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts one piece above the other. A REEL is a brisk Scottish folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cinema film of current events was shown before features in the days before television.

clue.text: Guide provides revolver, about £1 and upwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upwards turns the assembled letters backwards
the spinning toy goes about the money, enclosing it

parts.note: a top is a toy that revolves, spinning on its point
£ is L (from Latin libra) and 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A guide supplies a gun for about a pound, and more.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped 'about £1 and upwards'; the page prints it. 'revolver' wants to be a gun; it is a spinning top. TOP round LI gives TOLIP, which 'upwards' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot guides ships into harbour, and to pilot is to steer or lead.

clue.text: State requires fresh milk supplier?

parts.note: new means fresh, not used before
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow famous for rich milk

explanation.surface: A demand for new milk from a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the milk supplier is a cow, the Channel Island breed.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the original thirteen colonies, it is a US state on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Throws rare plant out

indicators.note: the letters of 'Throws rare' are put out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tossing an unusual plant out of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant out' reads as a gardening phrase, but 'plant' is the definition and 'out' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough-rooted European wild flower of the pea family, named for stopping the harrow.

clue.text: Something laid out beside bed linen

definitions.meaning: turf laid as grass next to a flower bed in a garden
a fine sheer cloth of flax or cotton

explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of mown grass sits beside a flower bed; separately, it is a fine woven fabric.

clue.text: £100 more collected by church for monument

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up and composed afresh into a new order

parts.note: £ is L (Latin libra) and 100 is the Roman numeral C

explanation.surface: An extra hundred pounds raised by a church for a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' signals that LC and MORE are rearranged, giving CROMLE, before CH is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric megalithic tomb of upright stones with a capstone, a dolmen.

clue.text: Relative lost head in river

indicators.note: the relative loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a brother is a male relative

explanation.surface: A family member drowned after losing his head in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rother is a river in southern England (there are several of the name).
explanation.definitionFit: A watercourse in Sussex and Kent, and another in Yorkshire, carries this name.

clue.text: Pudding-maker, has a good heart

indicators.note: the heart of the words is their inside, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: Someone who makes puddings is said to be kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a good heart' reads as praise, but 'heart' points inside 'has a good'.
explanation.definitionFit: The starch from a palm pith is cooked with milk into a traditional milk pudding.

clue.text: Put up lake plant to make type of gypsum

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the word up turns it backwards

parts.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Instructions to raise a lake plant to yield a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-grained, translucent white mineral, a form of gypsum, carved into ornaments.

clue.text: Point about river return, to many-it's unnecessary

annotationWithheld.why: Point about river return, to many—it's unnecessary: N + EED (DEE returned) gives NEED, but no reading makes 'to many' give LESS, so the clue as held does not parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Point about river return, to many-it's unnecessary

clue.text: Attendant has an unusually dismal day

indicators.note: the letters of 'dismal day' are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A servant is having an unusually gloomy day.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman servant who attends a noblewoman, helping her dress.

clue.text: Brave foe — but doesn't look it?

definitions.text: Brave foe — but doesn't look it?

parts.words: Brave foe — but doesn't look it?
parts.note: a Native American warrior's white enemy, whose white skin reads as fear

explanation.surface: An enemy who is courageous yet does not appear so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is the noun, a Native American warrior; the white settler foe looks pallid, as if afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns' term for a white person, the warriors' enemy, whose pallor suggests fright.

clue.text: Wound expert comes in later, perhaps

indicators.note: the expert comes into the middle of the other letters
the word later is only perhaps what is meant, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An injury specialist arrives later than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray S is an OCR blemish. 'perhaps' turns LATER into L...RATE, and 'comes in' puts ACE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear or gash flesh; to injure by ripping.

clue.text: Periods of bewilderment, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, not written

parts.note: a daze is a state of stunned bewilderment

explanation.surface: Spells of confusion, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Spans of time, as in 'in the old days', are periods.

clue.text: American poet's weather-forecasts ?

definitions.meaning: belonging to Robert, the New England poet of 'The Road Not Taken'
icy night conditions a weatherman predicts

explanation.definitionFit: The possessive of Robert the poet's surname; also the freezing spells a weatherman forecasts.

clue.text: Uncivilized character of Johnson's life?

definitions.meaning: Samuel Johnson wrote the Life of Richard, a poet of that name

explanation.definitionFit: A wild, barbarous person, and the poet Richard, subject of Samuel Johnson's biography.

clue.text: Object is to include the lines in full

indicators.note: the object takes the lines inside it

parts.note: an aim is an object or goal
BR, British Rail, ran the railway lines

explanation.surface: The goal is to cover all the lines completely.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stood for British Rail, Britain's state railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled to the brim, completely full.

clue.text: Stopped the others entering dear resort

indicators.note: the others go into the middle of the other letters
to re-sort the word dear is to rearrange its letters

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: The rest of the party arriving at a beloved holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but means sort again: DEAR becomes AR...ED around REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Halted, brought to a standstill; also taken into custody.

clue.text: How to win a girl from an East European climber

indicators.note: in a down clue a climber goes up, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a Pole is a European, a native of Poland

explanation.surface: Advice on courting a girl from a mountaineer of Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climber' turns EPOLE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away together to marry secretly is one way to win a bride.

clue.text: Top actor beginning to lack finish

indicators.note: the word lacks its finish, its final letter

parts.note: the start is the beginning

explanation.surface: A leading actor who begins but cannot finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading performer heads the cast and the billing.

clue.text: Pole joins a ship with sailor and master — retired diplomat

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a pole
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
AB, able seaman, is a sailor
MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A Pole, a ship's crew and its master join a diplomat who has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like the diplomat's status but turns RODASSABMA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The most senior envoy representing a state abroad.

clue.text: Rougher, we hear, before end of cay? Rubbish:

parts.note: rougher sounds like ruffer, a bridge player who ruffs, that is, plays a trump

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A coarser person, so we are told, came before the end of a reef: nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: To ruff at bridge is to play a trump; 'we hear' turns 'Rougher' into that player. A cay is a low island.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy but worthless stuff; nonsense.

clue.text: Duller summer after its beginning

indicators.note: the beginning of the word summer, its first letter

parts.note: an adder is one who sums

explanation.surface: Summer seems duller once it has started.
explanation.definitionFit: More gloomy, more melancholy.
